title: Two controllers + joseau11's aiming, rumble and auto-resume
intro: Needs TWO controllers and a second person. Start as the Arisen, no co-op running. Press End (keyboard) to start.

steps.text: Turning on two controllers, aiming, rumble and auto-resume; starting co-op with your main pawn.
PLAYER 2: hold L1 + L3 on your controller until it says it is set, then let go. Press End when done.
Sticks: each player moves on their own stick. Does each stick move only its own character?
Buttons: both attack, jump, sprint. Each controller only works its own character?
PLAYER 2's controller should rumble now (test pulse).
steps.each_frame: if not G_rb1 then G_rb1 = true; local R = _G.DPC_dbg.R; if R.rb_dev() then R.rb_pulse(0.8, 0.5) end end

steps.text: AIMING (unkillable goblins): markers over each player's target? P2: tap R3 = keep / free, flick right stick = next enemy, hold R3 = P1's target. P1: R3 = enemy nearest the screen centre.
RUMBLE: player 2 hits and gets hit, uses a skill, runs out of stamina. Does it rumble for each?
MENUS: player 1 opens the pause menu, then the map. Do DPC's markers and bars disappear while a menu is up?
AUTO-RESUME: player 2's pawn is downed now. A red Revive marker? Player 1 revives them; co-op should come back by itself with the same controllers. Press End once it has (or to move on).
Buttons mode 2 (leave the Arisen's buttons to the game, joseau11's way). Same button check: any difference?
Camera mode 2 (holds still while player 2 moves their right stick). Compare with before.
Ending co-op, everything off. Tell Claude what worked and what didn't.

probes.pads:
local R = _G.DPC_dbg and _G.DPC_dbg.R
if not R or not R.tp then return "no DPC dev" end
local t = R.tp
return string.format("pads=%d p1=%X p2=%X wait=%s on=%s p1b=%X p2b=%X game_b=%X masked=%d stick=%d cam=%d%s", t.n or 0, t.p1 or 0, t.p2 or 0,
  tostring(t.wait_release), tostring(R.tp_on()), (t.p1v and t.p1v.b) or 0, (t.p2v and t.p2v.b) or 0, t.game_b or 0,
  t.masked or 0, t.stick_fixes or 0, t.cam_fixes or 0, t.err and (" ERR " .. t.err) or "")
